tldr: Lighter news cycle (core items span roughly Nov 12–14) but notably severe: a destructive wiper campaign hit Check Point gateways via "PHP2Shell," two more zero-days (N-able N-central, UnrealIRCd) saw same-day/in-the-wild exploitation, and a new state-linked actor ("SilentAir") has been hijacking telecom infrastructure across Asia to intercept calls and SMS. 9 core items qualified; two AI-weaponization reports (ARTEX, CAIRN) round out the emerging-threats picture.

emerging.title: ARTEX: open-source AI pentest framework weaponized within weeks
emerging.description: An AI-agent pentesting framework released on GitHub in July was abused within weeks by China-nexus groups (VAPOR PANDA, Storm-0940, Storm-3358), hitting 200+ orgs and 2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants, plus criminal crypto-theft operators.

emerging.title: CAIRN: fully autonomous AI framework runs real intrusions
emerging.description: Unit 42 found China-nexus actor CL-STA-1238 running a customized AI attack framework end-to-end against 19 organizations — semiconductor, defense, and civil-society targets — confirming unauthorized access or data theft at 10, with minimal human oversight after each operation's goal was set.

items.title: "PHP2Shell" exploited in destructive Check Point Gateway attacks
items.description: Attackers chained CVE-2026-109618/109619 (PHP RCE) with local priv-esc CVE-2026-123039 to root Check Point Gateways, deploy backdoors, and run a wiper against Israeli orgs; a second, non-destructive wave hit multiple countries. Both flaws now on CISA's KEV list.

items.title: N-able N-central zero-day exploited within hours of PoC release
items.description: A researcher's PoC for "4EverAble2Shell," chaining an Apache Axis flaw with an N-central weakness, led to confirmed compromises (XMRig cryptominer) on at least 21 servers within five hours of publication — even on fully patched systems.

items.title: UnrealIRCd flaw actively exploited, added to CISA KEV
items.description: CVE-2026-114713, a command-injection bug via an unescaped IRCv3 message tag, lets regular users gain server/IRCOp authority. The project confirmed in-the-wild exploitation; CISA added it to the KEV catalog Nov 13. Update to 6.2.7.1.

items.title: Apify confirms customer data breach via credential-based intrusion
items.description: A compromised credential let an attacker pivot into other customer accounts Nov 9–10, exposing names, emails, salted password hashes, 2FA recovery codes, and partial card data for some of Apify's ~91,000 customers.

items.title: SilentAir: new state-linked actor hijacking mobile networks
items.description: Enea disclosed a previously unknown, likely state-level actor using SS7/Diameter signaling abuse from compromised telecom nodes to intercept calls and SMS across six-plus Asian countries (Taiwan the main target) plus a dozen others, tracked since 2025.

items.title: Law enforcement guts Gootloader, CastleRAT, StealC infrastructure
items.description: A DOJ/Europol-led Operation Endgame wave seized 235 servers and 257 domains and recovered 6.4 million victim credentials across three cybercrime-as-a-service malware families that fed ransomware and data-theft operations.

items.title: FAA ground stop: no sign of hacking, FBI probes software update
items.description: A nationwide FAA ground stop Nov 13 was traced to a crashed L3Harris air-traffic communications network following a software/equipment update, not a cyberattack, officials say; the FBI is still reviewing the update as a possible cause.

items.title: Citrix patches 10 critical NetScaler vulnerabilities
items.description: Citrix fixed 28 flaws (9 critical in ADC/Gateway, 1 critical auth-bypass in NetScaler Console) spanning memory overflows in packet, SMPP, DNS, OTP and ICA-proxy handling. No in-the-wild exploitation yet, but NetScaler is a frequent target — patch now.

items.title: Meta fined $887M in Italy over gallery photo access
items.description: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805M ($887M) for accessing Android users' photo galleries for Facebook suggestions without specific, informed consent — enabled by default and bundled into one broad permission. Meta has 60 days to comply.

action: Patch/update immediately: Check Point Gateways (PHP2Shell hotfix SK1000302), N-able N-central (apply latest patches, restrict Legacy API), UnrealIRCd (upgrade to 6.2.7.1), and Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway/Console (all 28 fixes, prioritize the 10 critical). All four are either under active exploitation or sit on internet-facing, frequently-targeted infrastructure.
